text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- COMESA's executive secretary Bingu wa Mutharika of Malawi, being investigated for alleged misconduct, has been temporarily replaced by Kenyan Joel Mwencha.
- A 17-member delegation from the Republic of China arrived in Malawi on Monday to discuss with the government and the private sector investment opportunities in the country.
- Malawi President Bakili Muluzi has been slammed by opposition parties for admitting in public that he offered cash and fertilizer to an opposition candidate during a by-election last November.
- The high court is to begin hearing murder trials in districts in a move to speed up long-standing cases, high court registrar Edward Twea said.
- Health and Population Minister Ziliro Chibambo has been rushed to a South African clinic with a spinal injury.
- Police headquarters has ordered the arrest of illegal aliens in all of the country's 25 districts.
